label: SIMULATION: virtual people generated from published norms and stated assumptions. Not clinical validation; no real participants.

assumptions.source: Assumption (the app targets people over about 40).

assumptions.assumption: Accommodation ~ Normal(Hofstetter mean 18.5 − 0.3·age, SD 0.75 D), clipped to [0, Hofstetter max 25 − 0.4·age].
assumptions.source: Hofstetter HW. A useful age-amplitude formula. Optom World 1950;38:42–45 (fitted to Duane 1912/1922). SD is an assumption: ±2 SD roughly spans Hofstetter's min–max envelope at ages 45–50.

assumptions.assumption: Hofstetter/Duane norms come from subjective push-up tests, which already include part of the depth of focus, so the main population may have slightly too much accommodation. A lower-amplitude population (centred on Hofstetter's minimum 15 − 0.25·age) is run as a sensitivity case.
Uncorrected spherical refractive error: mixture 72% N(+0.25, 0.5), 16% N(+1.5, 1.0), 12% N(−2.0, 1.25) D, clipped to [−6, +5]. Gives ≈10% below −1.00 D and ≈1% at or above +3.00 D.
assumptions.source: Assumption. Context: Kempen JH et al. Arch Ophthalmol 2004;122:495–505 (adults 40+: myopia ≤ −1 D ≈ 25%, hyperopia ≥ +3 D ≈ 10% in the US). We use a lower myopia share because people who already wear distance glasses are routed to an eye doctor by the safety questions; the high-hyperopia share is lower than Kempen's.

assumptions.assumption: Total depth of focus uniform 0.3–1.0 D per person (pupil-dependent). The app assumes 0.50 D.
assumptions.source: Wang B, Ciuffreda KJ. Depth-of-focus of the human eye: theory and clinical implications. Surv Ophthalmol 2006;51:75–85.

assumptions.assumption: Habitual reading distance ~ Normal(37, 5) cm, clipped to 25–55 cm.
assumptions.source: Bababekova Y et al. Font size and viewing distance of handheld smart phones. Optom Vis Sci 2011;88:795–797 (mean 36.2 cm for messages, 32.2 cm for web pages). SD is an assumption.

assumptions.assumption: Arm's reach for holding a phone uniform 55–70 cm; nothing beyond it can be measured. Closest measurable distance 12 cm (face must stay in frame).

Clear iff A − RE − DOF/2 ≤ 1/d ≤ A − RE + AA + DOF/2 (thin lens at the eye, vertex distance ignored, both eyes equal, no astigmatism, normal acuity, no eye disease). The constant-angle E removes letter-size cues, so only blur matters.
assumptions.source: Standard geometric optics; derivation in sim/README.md.

assumptions.assumption: Ideal readers A* = 1/W + RE − AA/2 (working distance in the middle of the clear range), rounded to 0.25 D.
assumptions.source: Stevens S. How to prescribe spectacles for near vision. Community Eye Health J 2019;32(107):47 ("keep half the accommodation in reserve").

assumptions.assumption: Refer if RE < -1.00 D (readers don't fix distance blur; a myopic shift after 60 can signal cataract) or ideal > +3.00; "no readers yet" if ideal < +0.75; otherwise in scope.
assumptions.source: Bench rule (task brief). Ready-made range +1.00..+3.00 from Stevens 2019.

assumptions.assumption: Camera distance relative error: shared per person (calibration / iris size) SD 4% + per reading SD 1%. Swept 0–8%, both shared and fully independent per reading.
assumptions.source: Google MediaPipe Iris (2020) reports 4.3% mean relative depth error (SD 2.4%) before calibration; ruler calibration should reduce the shared part. Split into shared/per-reading parts is an assumption.

assumptions.assumption: Each judged limit of clear vision (and each N6 check) has independent error SD 0.25 D. Swept 0–0.5 D.

At the rack: first pair = weaker of the app's two "try first" pairs (0.50 stock) or the starting strength (0.25 stock); follow assessTryOn()'s suggested change, snapped to stock (at least one step); stop at "good" or after 3 pairs and keep the best-centred. "Weaker" on +1.00 → no readers; "stronger" on +3.00 → refer.
assumptions.source: Assumption about how people use the try-on screen.

assumptions.assumption: Age table = Stevens 2019 Table 2 for 40 cm (as in src/core/optics.ts); the W-adjusted variant adds 1/W − 2.5 D using the camera-measured W. Neither can refer.

Rack card = an ideal blur meter: the smallest readable line reports the dioptres of blur where it is held, labelled blur + a fixed reserve (smallest line = +1.00; past +3.00 counted as refer). The reserve is chosen to maximise the card's own score at 14 in on this population (best case for the card). Held exactly at 35.6 cm, or at the person's own distance with 10% SD. Myopic blur reads as a need for plus. Change of letter angular size with distance is ignored.
assumptions.source: Assumption, deliberately generous to the card.

assumptions.assumption: No learning, fatigue or lighting effects; noise is independent between limits and pairs; people follow instructions.

strategies.label: Age table (40 cm)
strategies.description: Stevens 2019 age table for 40 cm; no measurement.

strategies.label: Age table + measured distance
strategies.description: Same table shifted to the camera-measured working distance; no near-point test.

strategies.label: Rack card at 14 in
strategies.description: Printed card held exactly at 35.6 cm as instructed (ignores where the person actually reads).

strategies.label: Rack card where they read
strategies.description: Printed card held around the person's own reading distance (SD 10%), read as if at 14 in.

strategies.label: Small Print start
strategies.description: recommend() on simulated noisy camera measurements, buying that exact strength (0.25 stock).

strategies.label: Small Print + try-on (0.50 stock)
strategies.description: recommend() then assessTryOn() at a rack with 0.50 steps, max 3 pairs.

strategies.label: Small Print + try-on (0.25 stock)
strategies.description: recommend() then assessTryOn() at a rack with 0.25 steps, max 3 pairs.

strategies.label: What-if: try-on + probe pair (0.50 stock)
strategies.description: NOT shipped. Shipped assessTryOn(); when the far end is out of reach, try a pair 0.50 D stronger to measure it before accepting.

strategies.label: What-if: try-on + probe pair (0.25 stock)
strategies.description: NOT shipped. As above with 0.25 stock.

strategies.label: What-if: far end estimated from lens power (0.50 stock)
strategies.description: NOT shipped, rejected. assessTryOn() variant that estimates an out-of-reach far end as strength − DOF/2 (assumes no refractive error).

strategies.label: Reference: ideal pair, 0.50 stock
strategies.description: The true ideal snapped to 0.50 steps: the best any method can do with 0.50 stock.
